messages:
Morgan: Heads-up — seeing a ~20% p95 latency regression when KV prefetch + continuous batching is on for replay runs on H100 vs A100. Repro steps and numbers below. Need a short parity checklist so we can isolate kernel selection vs runtime behaviour.
Carla: Ugh. Can you paste the numbers and which images/drivers you used? :eyes:
Morgan: Quick paste:
```
Replay run: 2026-03-10 14:02Z
Model: rdx-2.1-bert-serve
Workload: chat-style replay (avg seq 256, tail 1024), 8k requests
A100 (driver 525.89, image rdx-runtime:2026-02-20): p50=45ms p95=210ms tokens/sec=32k
H100 (driver 535.101, image rdx-runtime:2026-03-02): p50=48ms p95=260ms tokens/sec=26k
Change: KV prefetch=true, batching window=8ms, continuous batching on
```
Morgan: When I flip KV prefetch off, H100 numbers align with A100 within 5%.
Raj: Interesting — could be kernel selector choosing a different matmul/attention kernel because of sequence-length distribution after prefetch. Also H100 math libraries behave differently with small batches.
Sasha: Did you confirm the kernel flags and env vars are identical? e.g. `RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT=auto`, `TF32_ALLOW=1`, `CUFFT_WORKSPACE=auto` — tiny differences blow up.
Morgan: I ran both with the same env snapshot except the driver and image tags above. Full env dump attached to the run. DevOps Bot: automated-run #1899993210 finished: exit=0, artifacts: /ci/artifacts/1899993210/; perf trace uploaded.
Carla: Can you try a synthetic run (no replay) with identical batch distribution to confirm it's replay-specific? We should get apples-to-apples.
Morgan: Will do. Synthetic run command I'm going to use:
```
python -m bench.synthetic --model rdx-2.1-bert-serve --seq-dist "mix:0.7:128,0.2:256,0.1:1024" --device h100 --driver 535.101 --image rdx-runtime:2026-03-02 --kv-prefetch true --batch-window-ms 8 --duration 10m
```
Morgan: If synthetic reproduces, then kernel/runtime path is the culprit. If not, replay harness interaction (cache warmup/eviction) might matter.
Raj: Also collect kernel selection logs: `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_selector,kv` — that will print which kernel variant was chosen per layer.
Sasha: Good call. And capture NVTX ranges + CUPTI counters. On H100 I often see attention kernel fallback to generic kernel for seq>512 depending on kernel flags.
Eric: A couple of hypotheses: 1) KV prefetch reorders memory accesses causing larger temporary allocations -> different kernel chosen; 2) batching window interacts with continuous batching and increases average batch size on H100 because of faster single-token throughput, changing kernel heuristics.
Carla: For parity plan:
- matrix of (GPU types: A100,H100) x (driver: 525,535) x (image tags: 2026-02-20, 2026-03-02) x (kv-prefetch on/off) x (batch-window 4/8/16ms)
- run small 10k req synthetic with same seq distribution and collect kernel_selector logs + nvprof
- if regression persists on H100, capture `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_bindings` and run filtered nsight snapshot of the worst layers
- if only in replay, add a replay-only instrument to log KV hit/evict + prefix cache occupancy per request
Morgan: I'll kick off the matrix but want a prioritized minimal repro first: (H100, driver 535, image 2026-03-02, kv-prefetch on, batch-window 8ms) vs same with kv-prefetch off.
DevOps Bot: queued job 1899993210-a (H100,kv-on) and 1899993210-b (H100,kv-off). ETA ~18m.
Raj: When you have traces, grep for `kernel_variant=gemm_fused_*` and `attention_impl=fast_fwd` — differences there point to kernel selection. Also check `SM version` printed by kernel logs (sm_90 vs sm_80).
Sasha: If kernel selection differs, try forcing kernel_policy=prefer_sm90 or `RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT=sm90` to test whether forcing makes H100 behave like A100 numbers. That will confirm selector heuristics.
Morgan: Early results from queued jobs: kv-on p95=268ms, kv-off p95=215ms on H100. So KV prefetch definitely correlates.
Carla: Next step: profile memory traffic around KV prefetch: look for memcpy peaks and whether prefetch causes cudaMemcpyAsync in the critical path. Also examine whether prefetch increases L2 thrash.
Eric: Another quick check: run with `RUNTIME_BATCHING=off` on H100 with kv-on. If regression goes away, it's the batching+kv interaction.
Morgan: Good idea. I'll add that job.
Raj: Logging note — ensure traces include the batch-size distribution per 1s window. The selector heuristics use recent batch histograms; a slight skew can change kernel decisions.
Sasha: Also keep an eye on cuda scheduler preemption behavior — driver versions differ in preemption heuristics which can affect latency tails with many small kernels.
Carla: For the parity doc we should add a short checklist template so SREs can run this when a new driver/image lands. I can draft and push to the playbook if you folks agree.
Morgan: Yes please. I want a reproducible minimal test and a follow-up mitigation: either tweak kernel selector thresholds for kv-prefetch path or add an opt-out knob for prefetch on H100 until upstream libraries stabilize.
Eric: If we end up adjusting selector thresholds, include unit tests in the harness that assert p95 within X% across GPU types for canonical workloads. Otherwise regressions will slip through.
Carla: Agreed. I'll draft the playbook and add the matrix command snippets + what to collect (kernel logs, nvtx, CUPTI, batch histograms, KV occupancy, container diff).
Morgan: Thanks — will report back with the full trace links. :thumbsup:
DevOps Bot: job 1899993210-c (H100 kv-on batching-off) finished: p95=216ms, tokens/sec improved. Artifact: /ci/artifacts/1899993210-c/trace.nvtx.zip
Morgan: Looks like batching+kv interaction is the most likely root cause. Next: reproduce kernel selection change with a focused synthetic microbenchmark and then propose selector tweak.
Carla: Great. Keep the thread updated. If you want I'll also add a small entry to the weekly eng-runtime sync agenda to review selector changes. :coffee:
